# Marriott.com Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/marriott-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/marriott-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects hotel data from Marriott.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [Scraping Marriott Hotel Prices and Availability (2026)](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-marriott)
- **Code:** [`marriott.py`](marriott.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Hotel](results/hotel.json) · [Search](results/search.json)

## What it scrapes

- Marriott hotel search for finding hotels in a destination for given dates:
    - hotel name, brand, location, distance, rating and review count, thumbnail, lowest price
- Marriott hotel details for:
    - address, phone, description, check-in and check-out times, pet and smoking policies

## Functions

- `scrape_search(city, from_date, to_date, num_rooms=1, num_adults=2)` → `List[MarriottProperty]`: Scrape Marriott city search for the property list.
- `scrape_hotels(property_ids)` → `List[MarriottHotel]`: Scrape hotel details for the given Marriott property ids.

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields:

- **`MarriottProperty`**: `marriott_id`, `name`, `url`, `brand?`, `latitude?`, `longitude?`, `distance_meters?`, `description?`, `review_rating?`, `review_count?`, `thumbnail?`, `bookable?`, `currency?`, `lead_price?`
- **`MarriottHotel`**: `marriott_id`, `name?`, `url?`, `brand?`, `latitude?`, `longitude?`, `currency?`, `bookable?`, `address?`, `city?`, `state?`, `postal_code?`, `country?`, `phone?`, `description?`, `check_in?`, `check_out?`, `smoke_free?`, `pets_allowed?`, `pets_policy?`, `parking?`, `review_rating?`, `review_count?`, `airports?`

A field marked `?` can be `null`.

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`marriott.py`](marriott.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `asp` = `True`: Anti Scraping Protection, the earlier name of the [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker)
- `render_js` = `True`: render the page in a real browser
- `country` = `"US"`: country of the proxy
- `proxy_pool` = `"public_residential_pool"`: proxy pool (datacenter or residential)

## Notes

Marriott.com can be difficult to scrape because of scraper blocking and heavy JavaScript rendering, so this scraper uses Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker) feature with JavaScript rendering and residential proxies.

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/marriott-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_search_scraping`, `test_hotel_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
